name: Dielectric Vitreous Humor Agitator DVHA-2 'Snowglobe'
description:
The DVHA-2 exploits a specific vulnerability of the biological eye: the vitreous humor, the gel-like fluid filling the posterior chamber of the eyeball, is a dielectric medium with a distinct electrical permittivity that differs measurably from surrounding tissue. By projecting a rapid-cycling dielectric field tuned to this permittivity differential, the weapon induces micro-agitation within the vitreous humor — essentially causing the gel to vibrate at a frequency that generates internal pressure waves against the retina and the posterior lens. The immediate effect is severe visual disruption: targets experience a blizzard of phosphene flashes, cascading floaters, and a complete loss of coherent image formation for several minutes.

At higher power settings, the DVHA-2's agitation effect can cause partial vitreous detachment — the gel pulling away from the retinal surface — which produces longer-duration visual impairment and, in some cases, permanent retinal complications. Tessera Corponation's medical division originally developed the underlying dielectric targeting technology for ophthalmic surgery, specifically for non-contact manipulation of intraocular structures. The weapons application emerged from a defense contract that Tessera has since officially terminated, though production of the DVHA-2 continues through a subsidiary operating under a different name.

The weapon's street name 'Snowglobe' comes from how affected targets describe their visual experience: a chaotic swirl of bright specks and moving shapes, as if their vision had been shaken like a decorative snow globe. The name has also been applied metaphorically in GLMZ street slang — to 'snowglobe' someone means to thoroughly disorient them, whether through the weapon or through information overload and deception.
specifications: effective range: 1–35 meters power source: Compact dielectric field generator cell, 25 shots per charge effect duration standard: 3–7 minutes complete visual disruption effect duration high power: Potential partial vitreous detachment; impairment up to 48 hours weight: 1.4 kg form factor: Compact sidearm profile with adjustable power dial targeting requirement: Must achieve line-of-sight to target's eye region; effective through standard eyewear; blocked by opaque face shields augmentation note: Fully cybernetic ocular replacements are immune; biological eyes with implanted lenses retain partial vulnerability
tactical_use: The DVHA-2 is a precision blinding tool, most effective in engagements where temporarily removing a target's vision creates a decisive advantage without generating a lethal outcome. Extraction teams use it to blind security personnel at key moments �� a three-minute vision blackout is enough to move a person through a checkpoint. Close-protection operatives carry it as a first-response tool to create distance from an attacker. In competitive underworld contexts, it is used to humiliate rather than harm — 'snowglobing' a rival in public, leaving them stumbling and helpless, is a specific form of social violence. High-power use as a permanent blinding tool is illegal even under its restricted license, a line that operators cross with increasing frequency.
cultural_context: The DVHA-2 sits at an interesting intersection in GLMZ's weapon culture. Its restricted-legal status means it appears in both sanctioned security contexts and criminal ones, and the same weapon model is carried by corporate bodyguards and street enforcers alike. The metaphorical use of 'snowglobe' in the city's slang has given the weapon a cultural presence beyond its physical use — media, information brokers, and con artists all use the term. Among the augmentation-reliant community, the weapon represents a specific anxiety about the value of unaugmented biological senses: your eyes are a vulnerability that money can solve, and those who haven't spent that money know it. Tessera Corponation's continued involvement through subsidiaries is an open secret that the city's investigative press has reported on repeatedly without legal consequence.
known_users: Street-level enforcers specializing in non-lethal dominance
Intelligence operatives requiring temporary target incapacitation
story_hooks: Someone has modified a batch of DVHA-2s to lock permanently on high-power mode with the safety override removed. The units are indistinguishable from standard models until fired. They're already in circulation.

A Tessera Corponation subsidiary has been quietly approached by a buyer wanting DVHA-2 units in quantities that suggest crowd deployment — not individual use. The subsidiary contact wants out and needs help disappearing.

Three witnesses to a major corporate crime have all independently reported sudden severe visual impairment that their doctors can't explain through any standard cause. The symptom profile matches high-power DVHA-2 exposure.

A black-market ophthalmologist is offering a vitreous humor replacement procedure that provides immunity to the DVHA-2 — the synthetic gel she's using is proprietary, and its origin traces back to Tessera's original ophthalmic surgery program in ways that shouldn't be possible.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, clinical sidearm with an almost surgical aesthetic — compact and precise rather than aggressive. The weapon has an asymmetrical profile dominated by a bulbous, translucent emitter head that dominates the muzzle end, giving it an unnerving resemblance to an oversized eye itself. The emitter chamber is the visual anchor of the design, a faintly luminescent polycarbonate dome that suggests fragility despite being hardened polymer. The grip tapers smoothly into the body, engineered for precision rather than raw control.
physical_description.dimensions: 24 cm length overall, 18 cm barrel-to-emitter-tip, 6 cm grip width. The emitter head occupies 8 cm of forward length and 5 cm in diameter at its widest point.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light — 1.4 kg feels almost insubstantial in the hand, like holding medical instrumentation rather than a weapon. The weight distribution is front-heavy due to the emitter assembly, creating an odd balance that requires conscious adjustment.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer chassis with reinforced polycarbonate emitter dome. Internal field-projection array uses precision-cut ceramic matrices and micro-etched copper conductors.
physical_description.finish: Satin white and clinical grey, with a faint nacreous sheen across the emitter housing that shifts subtly under light. The grip section is matte charcoal with micro-texturing. No weathering in stock condition — this is a tool meant to look pristine and trustworthy.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominantly off-white and clinical grey with translucent amber accents visible within the emitter dome where field-generation matrices are visible. Accent trim in brushed nickel at control points.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with shallow vertical ribbing — designed for precision two-finger control rather than full-handed grip. Slightly tacky to prevent slippage, almost medical-glove smooth.
distinctive_features: Translucent polycarbonate emitter dome revealing glowing field-matrix arrays within
Adjustable power dial on left side marked with power increments and a red 'HIGH' threshold warning zone
Micro-LED status indicator strip running along the top — cycles through green (charged), amber (active), red (safety engaged)
Fine cross-hair etching on the emitter dome surface for targeting reference
Subtle Tessera Corporation medical-division marking (stylized 'T' with ophthalmology symbol) engraved on grip
Dielectric field-bleed indicator — faint aurora-like shimmer visible around emitter in low light when powered
Recessed charging port on rear grip styled like medical equipment connectors
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Corporation's stylized 'T' logo with embedded ophthalmology rod symbol engraved discreetly on the grip. Serial number plate mounted on the left side in small, clinical typeface. The subsidiary production designation is stamped internally only.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-used units show minimal visual wear — scuffed grip texturing, faint scratches on the emitter dome from careful handling, micro-wear on the power dial from repeated adjustments. Battle-worn examples develop stress fractures around the emitter base and discoloration in the polycarbonate from repeated field-cycling. Well-maintained examples retain full translucency; neglected weapons develop a milky, stress-marked emitter.
